Hypothesis: In biliary tract cancer, specific DDR gene alterations result in the accumulation of cytosolic DNA that triggers the cGAS-STING pathway, thereby generating a robust interferon response which induces PD-L1 upregulation. This, in turn, promotes T cell recruitment, converting the tumor microenvironment from immunologically cold to hot. Utilizing state-of-the-art real-time genomic and transcriptomic profiling enables the identification of BTC tumors with this DDR-immune activation signature. In a critical extension to the original concept, we propose that administration of PARP inhibitors will further compromise DDR, thus intensifying the cascade of immune activation. To address the potential dual role of PD-L1 and ensure that its upregulation results in beneficial T cell infiltration rather than disproportionate immune suppression, our hypothesis incorporates an adaptive treatment stratification framework driven by continuous biomarker monitoring. This refined approach not only preserves the original causal chain but also enhances its clinical implementability by integrating preclinical validation stages, detailed immune phenotyping, and pragmatic real-time monitoring to optimize dosing and scheduling of combination therapies with ICIs.
Abstract: We hypothesize that in biliary tract cancer (BTC), specific alterations in DNA damage repair (DDR) genes initiate a cascade wherein cytosolic DNA accumulates, thereby triggering the cGAS-STING pathway. This activation elicits a robust interferon response that upregulates PD-L1, leading to enhanced T cell recruitment and reprogramming of the tumor microenvironment from immunologically cold to hot. Our strategy leverages continuous, real-time genomic and transcriptomic profiling to dynamically identify and stratify tumors exhibiting this DDR‐immune activation signature. Furthermore, the use of PARP inhibitors is proposed to further exacerbate DDR impairment, thereby amplifying the cytosolic DNA accrual and subsequent immune activation. By incorporating adaptive biomarker monitoring to account for potential counter-regulatory effects (e.g., PD-L1 driven immune evasion) and modulating treatment parameters such as dosage and scheduling, this approach aims to optimize the combination therapy of PARP inhibitors with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) for enhanced therapeutic outcomes in BTC.
CausalChain: DDR gene alterations -> Cytosolic DNA accumulation -> cGAS-STING activation -> Interferon signaling -> PD-L1 upregulation -> T cell recruitment -> Conversion of tumor microenvironment (cold to hot) -> Enhanced sensitivity to ICIs; PARP inhibition -> Further DDR impairment -> Amplified immune activation
